observations: Net gamma exposure is positive: dealers are long gamma and hedge against the direction of price moves
Spot trades above the zero-gamma level and just under the call wall, so the market sits on the long-gamma side of the flip point with the nearest reference level directly overhead
The put wall is well below spot; the reference range between the walls is wide on the downside and narrow on the upside
The twenty-five delta put skew is inside GaleCore's calm zone and the wing premium over the at-the-money is modest
The volatility index is in the mid teens and the vol-of-vol index is subdued, consistent with a market that is not pricing an imminent shock
implications: With dealers long gamma, hedging flows should dampen intraday moves and favour mean reversion, so realized volatility is expected to stay contained
The call wall sitting just above spot is where hedging resistance would first be expected; the flip point below is the level whose loss would change the character of hedging flows
A calm skew alongside positive gamma is a coherent combination: the options market is not paying up for protection while hedging flows are counter-cyclical

evidence.claim: Net GEX is positive, dealers are long gamma

limitations: Intraday read taken during the cash session for end-to-end evidence regeneration; it is not a daily record of the series
The skew snapshot carries no GaleCore timestamp; it reflects the moment of the request
VIX and VVIX are the latest prints at the time of the request and will move through the session
GEX reflects current open interest and coverage and will shift with the session's flow
No comparison with earlier sessions is made here; such comparisons are only valid through the query step
